label: steps 3-5 of a sequence that began with q
explanation: Fires at steps t=3..5, during the original phase or on the <DEL> input, in sequences whose first original token is q. first_tok=q holds about 94% of the activation mass (24x lift). The input token at the current step barely matters. Magnitude is largest at t=4 and drops off at t=5; the strongest examples also have q as the second token (q q ...). It never fires at t<=2, at t>=6, or in the copy phase. Missed activations are weak (5.9% of mass), mostly sequences with q in second position. False positives are mostly at t=5 or on short sequences where <DEL> falls at t=4/5.

issues: Systematic false-positive class: a <DEL> input at t=5 (L=5). With first_tok=q, t=5 and phase==1, precision is 0.069 (2733 predicted steps, about 93% inactive). That is roughly 38% of the predicate's dev false positives. The explanation says the feature fires 'on the <DEL> input', but that only holds for <DEL> at t=3 (precision 0.77) and t=4 (precision 0.82). It does not hold at t=5.
The explanation says FPs come from 'short sequences where <DEL> falls at t=4 or 5'. Only t=5 is a real FP class. <DEL> at t=4 mostly fires.

Positional profile confirmed: precision is 0.989 at t=3 and 0.969 at t=4, but only 0.65 at t=5 in the original phase. Mass is t=3 0.445, t=4 0.476, t=5 0.078. The magnitude claim holds: largest at t=4 (top examples peak there), weaker at t=5.
'Never fires at t>=6' is almost true: 92 active steps at t=6 on dev (0.1% of mass), e.g. 'q q g k d i' firing at step 6. This is negligible.
Copy-phase silence confirmed: phase==2 has 0 active steps.
Misses are scattered rather than systematic. orig(1)==q with first_tok!=q at t=3..5 has precision 0.16 and holds 5% of mass. Other misses are tiny activations with assorted first tokens.
The first_tok=q dependence is confirmed: 94% of mass, 24x lift. in_tok is flat (about 1.0-1.3x lift).
